kypExtensions.summary: The member-facing synthesis of the six printed plans: three axes — NETWORK (EPO/HMO in-network only, with EPO's printed emergency exception; PoS/PPO allow out-of-network care), REFERRAL (HMO and PoS print the primary care gate; PPO alone prints 'no referral requirement'), and the premium-vs-out-of-pocket SEE-SAW (HMO prints both ends low; HDHP prints premium low / out-of-pocket high with its HSA pairing) — plus the two rows outside the grid by design (ACO = provider-side coordination for Medicare patients; HDHP = pure cost design). The grid explicitly marks the page's silences: NO referral or cost rule is printed for EPO, and NO network/referral rules for ACO or HDHP — the decoder marks them '— not printed' rather than inventing rules.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints six parallel rows of rules; the three-axis grid, the see-saw reading, the hybrid reading of PoS, the provider-side vs cost-design classification of ACO/HDHP, and the silence-marking convention are KYP's organization of the printed facts.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea QUESTION 1 + mechanisms[0] network-referral-cost-map + blocks[4] the plan decoder + Zone A of the registry visual

kypExtensions.summary: The payer-facing synthesis of the five printed payment models: one ladder ordered by UNIT of payment — PER SERVICE (fee-for-service; discounted fee-for-service is the same unit at a rate predetermined by providers and payers, eg, PPOs), PER SERVICE DIVIDED among all providers and facilities involved (bundled payment, 'regardless of ultimate cost'), PER INCIDENT of care (global payment — the elective-surgery model covering surgery plus the necessary pre- and postoperative visits), PER PATIENT-PER-PERIOD (capitation, 'regardless of how much the patient uses the healthcare system,' used by some HMOs) — with the rule that the wider the unit, the more utilization risk shifts from payer to provider. The ladder arrangement is KYP's (the printed table lists the rows alphabetically).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints five parallel definitions; the unit-of-payment ladder, the risk-bearer assignment on each rung, and the payer-to-provider risk-shift rule are KYP's synthesis. The two printed cross-table ties (discounted FFS 'eg, PPOs'; capitation 'used by some HMOs') are the source's own and are carried as printed.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea QUESTION 2 + mechanisms[1] risk-bearer-map + blocks[5] the payment-model decoder + Zone B of the registry visual

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the EPO emergency-visit stem, the capitation fixed-per-patient stem, the elective-surgery global-payment stem, the ESRD-vs-limited-income eligibility stem), 4 traps (HMO vs PPO gate-and-see-saw; EPO vs HMO; Medicare vs Medicaid; capitation vs bundled vs global units), 3 pivots (the PER-WHAT router for payment-model option lists; the age/disability/ESRD-vs-income door router; the referral-silence tell — only rows that PRINT a referral rule can be tested on it), and a 10-card recall set covering all six plans, all five models, and both programs.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the plan and model definitions only; the attack structure, distractor pairings, the silence-trap, and the question shapes are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The mnemonic ledger: First Aid's OWN two mnemonics, printed in the Medicare-and-Medicaid block's RIGHT panel — 'MedicarE is for Elderly.' / 'MedicaiD is for Disadvantaged.' and 'The 4 parts of Medicare:' (A hospital Admissions incl. hospice and skilled nursing; B Basic medical bills; C parts A + B = Combo delivered by approved private companies; D prescription Drugs) — carried VERBATIM and ATTRIBUTED in the mnemonics array, the memory callout, the verbatim text block, and the visual's split panel; plus TWO KYP originals, marked as such: 'HMO GATES AND SAVES; PPO ROAMS AND PAYS' (the six-plan axis) and 'PER SERVICE, PER INCIDENT, PER PATIENT — the wider the PER, the more risk shifts to the provider' (the payment ladder).
kypExtensions.rationale: The two panel mnemonics are the source's own (attributed, not counted as KYP's); their red keyword-letter printing is FA-own furniture (VLM-adjudicated: two 240dpi zoom passes read the letters in red, governing over the 120dpi full-page pass that called the panel plain black); the two ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[9] the memory callout + blocks[3] the verbatim text block + Zone C of the registry visual

kypExtensions.summary: The clinical anchor layer: the ESRD door (end-stage renal disease qualifies a patient of ANY age for Medicare — the nephrology bridge), the HSA pairing printed with the HDHP, the elective-surgery episode printed with global payment (one payment owning the preoperative visit, the surgery, and the postoperative visits), and the referral workflow (HMO and PoS members route through primary care before specialists; the PPO's 'no referral requirement' is the counterweight) — plus the boundary framing (the Healthcare Delivery arc: disease prevention and prophylaxis on book 276 before this page; palliative care and medical errors on book 278 after it) and the miniCase (the self-employed consultant wanting the lowest premiums + a tax-advantaged account, routed to HDHP with HSA against HMO, PPO, EPO, and ACO distractors).
kypExtensions.rationale: The eligibility rules and examples themselves are printed (FA-own); the anchor organization, the workflow framing, the boundary framing, and the miniCase vignette with its four distractors are KYP's design, flagged as such.
